metadata.note: The Vermont Valley Railroad, Brattleboro VT - Dummerston - Putney - East Putney - Westminster - Bellows Falls VT, about 24 mi entirely in Vermont on the west bank of the Connecticut, opened 23 June 1851. One physical line drawn as one feature per operator era on identical geometry (CLAUDE.md Rule 4 splits): Vermont Valley 1851-1865, Vermont Central 1871-1872, Central Vermont 1873-1876, Connecticut River Railroad 1880-1892, Boston and Maine 1893-1966. Built from research/branches/vermont_valley_railroad.txt (researched 2026-10-15).
metadata.colour_note: The Vermont Valley Railroad colour is shared with the 'Vermont Valley Railroad' feature (vermont-valley-sullivan-bellows-falls-windsor) in the pending, unmerged Sullivan County Railroad layer (dataset branch claude/add-sullivan-county-railroad), from which it was pulled programmatically. If that layer's colour changes before merge, change this one with it.
omitted: 1865-1870: the road was leased in 1865 to Rutland & Burlington interests (RRHS: the R&B company, 12 May 1865; de.Wikipedia: two private entrepreneurs involved with the R&B, 1 June 1865, the Rutland company taking over lease and operation only on 23 Jan 1871). No source names whose crews and engines ran the trains, and no timetable snapshot falls in these years, so the span is left undrawn rather than coloured with a guessed operator (and no R&B or Rutland feature is created on this evidence).

1877-1879 (to 30 June 1880): passenger service almost certainly continued, but no source names who ran the trains -- candidates are the Vermont Valley of 1871 after regaining its line on 5 April 1877 (de.Wikipedia), the Connecticut River RR 'taking control' from 1877 (de.Wikipedia), or the Central Vermont continuing to 1880 (en.Wikipedia Union Station). Left undrawn, matching the Sullivan County layer, which omits the same years for the same reason.

Amtrak (Montrealer 1972-1987 and 1989-1995, Vermonter from 1995): already drawn as amtrak-90 in amtrak.geojson; not duplicated. The 1924-1966 Montrealer/Washingtonian through train is drawn separately in montrealer.geojson.
metadata.freight_only_audit: Built to Rule 1: the B&M feature ends with passenger service in 1966; post-1966 freight (B&M, Central Vermont from 1988, New England Central from 1994/95) is mentioned in notes only.
not_yet_sourced: 1865-1870 operator (see omitted): whether the Rutland & Burlington / Rutland company or private lessees ran the trains; lease day 12 May vs 1 June 1865.

1877-1880 operator (see omitted), and when the Central Vermont lease actually ended: 1876 (American-Rails.com), 5 Apr 1877 (de.Wikipedia), or 1880 (en.Wikipedia Union Station, Lindsell p.173). ICC Valuation Reports vol. 30 (Google Books GO1DAAAAIAAJ), Lindsell's Rail Lines of Northern New England pp.171-173, or the Vermont Railroad Commissioner's reports for 1877-1880 would likely settle it.
The pre-1913 Brattleboro terminal alignment, before the ICC's 0.72-mi extension of 1913-14 (geometry at the Brattleboro end is a later alignment for 1851-1912).
Date of the Bellows Falls tunnel relative to the 1851 opening (not checked).
Incorporation day of the Vermont Valley of 1871: 29 July (ICC) vs 3 July (de.Wikipedia). Not a map date.
1880 agency-agreement day: 1 July (Vermont Valley, ICC) vs 31 Aug (Sullivan, ICC). Year firm.
Day of the 1966 end: 6 Sept (en.Wikipedia Bellows Falls station) vs 3/4 Sept. Year firm.
All headway_min and avg_speed_kmh values are estimates; no pre-1951 timetable was read for frequency, and the 1951 Guide OCR does not separate daily from non-daily trains.
sources: Official Guide of the Railways, February 1952 (schedules of Sept 1951), Boston and Maine Table 16 'Connecticut River Line' and station index (research/sources/official_guide_1952.txt in the site repository)

geometry_source: OpenStreetMap: New England Central Railroad main track Brattleboro - Bellows Falls (ways tagged operator=New England Central Railroad, old_railway_operator=B&M; members of route relation 9048140) -- https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/9048140
properties.geometry_quality: Real-traced from OpenStreetMap: shortest-path routing (opstrace.py) over the New England Central Railroad's active main track (the Amtrak Vermonter's route), waypoints Brattleboro station, Dummerston (hand-pinned to the track; Nominatim returned the town centroid 4 km inland on the West River grade), Putney, East Putney, Westminster and Bellows Falls station. Of the routed length, 23.3 mi runs on ways tagged old_railway_operator=B&M and 0.2 mi on untagged NECR main track; no straight-line legs, no rail-trail or OpenHistoricalMap ways used. Traced 23.6 mi from the south end of Brattleboro station (where new_london_northern_railroad.geojson cv-new-london-brattleboro ends) to the north side of Bellows Falls station (the first point of the Sullivan / Rutland & Burlington layers, about 0.15 mi past the station, where the Sullivan line turns east to cross the Connecticut), against a documented 23.7 mi station-to-station (John Fowler's B&M mileposts 60.3 to 84.0) and 24.443 mi of road (ICC valuation, which includes a 0.72-mi extension in Brattleboro built 1913-14). CAVEAT (CLAUDE.md Rule 2): this is the MODERN alignment drawn back to 1851. At the Brattleboro end it is a LATER alignment than the 1851-1912 era: the ICC records a 0.72-mi 'extension in the city of Brattleboro' built 1913-14 (the period of the 1915 union station), and the pre-1913 terminal arrangement at Brattleboro has not been established, so roughly the southern 0.7 mi is drawn on the post-1914 layout for all features before then. The second main track Putney - Bellows Falls (~14 mi, 1901-03, ICC) does not move a centre-line trace. The Bellows Falls tunnel at the north end has not been dated against a source here; no other realignment has been checked and no period valuation map was consulted.

segments.note: The Vermont Valley Railroad (Vermont charter 8 Nov 1848) was 'placed in operation on June 23, 1851' (ICC valuation; Tuttle 1929: 'not opened for business until June 1851'; de.Wikipedia: second half of 1851), closing the last gap in the Springfield - Brattleboro - Bellows Falls - Burlington all-rail route. The company ran its own trains: superintendents Peyton R. Chandler and later Madison Sloat, general offices and the only machine shop at Bellows Falls, and in 1854 a single passenger conductor (Deming) on the Brattleboro run (Tuttle); its trains did not run north of Bellows Falls, where passengers changed cars. From 29 Sept 1855 the property was held by trustees for the bondholders (ICC) -- same company, no other operator named, so not split. Ends with the lease of the road to Rutland & Burlington interests in 1865: 12 May 1865 (Rutland Railroad Historical Society timeline) vs 1 June 1865 (de.Wikipedia, 'two entrepreneurs also involved in the R&B', ten years) -- day conflict, year firm. Sept 1861 - 1866 the Vermont Valley also leased the Sullivan Railroad; that is drawn on the Sullivan layer, not here. Headway is an ESTIMATE: no timetable for this era was read; one passenger conductor in 1854 suggests about two round trips a day.
sources: Segment-level: 1851 start from the ICC valuation report (23 June 1851) and Tuttle (1929); 1854 operation from Tuttle; 1865 end from the RRHS timeline (12 May 1865) and de.Wikipedia (1 June 1865). Headway not sourced.

segments.note: The Rutland Railroad, with its leases of the Vermont Valley and the Vermont & Massachusetts, was leased to the Vermont Central for 20 years from 1 January 1871 (Rutland Railroad Historical Society timeline; en.Wikipedia 'Central Vermont Railway'); de.Wikipedia has the Rutland taking over the Vermont Valley lease and its operation on 23 Jan 1871 and sub-leasing it to the Vermont Central. The Vermont Valley itself was reorganized as the Vermont Valley Railroad Company of 1871 that summer (29 July per ICC, 3 July per de.Wikipedia) -- not an operator change, the line being under lease. The company was renamed Central Vermont in 1872/73; the split into a separate feature from 1873 follows the colour convention already in vermont_central_railroad.geojson, not an operator change. Headway is an ESTIMATE: no timetable for this era was read for frequency.
sources: Segment-level: 1 Jan 1871 start from the RRHS timeline and en.Wikipedia 'Central Vermont Railway' (de.Wikipedia: 23 Jan 1871); 1872 end = the Vermont Central / Central Vermont rename as split in vermont_central_railroad.geojson. Headway not sourced.

segments.note: The same lease under the company's new name, Central Vermont; with the Vermont & Massachusetts and the Rutland also under lease it controlled a through route Burlington - Bellows Falls - Brattleboro ('the three lines became part of the Central Vermont Railway in 1873', en.Wikipedia 'Union Station (Brattleboro)', citing Lindsell). John Fowler's 1876 Pathfinder column lists Dummerston, Putney, East Putney and Westminster -- positive evidence of passenger stops in 1876. Drawn to 1876, the shortest-supported end. SOURCE CONFLICT on when the Central Vermont let go: 1876 (American-Rails.com, uncited: it 'discontinued its lease of both the Sullivan County and Vermont Valley railroads'; matches the Sullivan's 1876); 5 April 1877 (de.Wikipedia: the Vermont Valley of 1871 acquired its line, the leases were dissolved and the Connecticut River RR took control); 1880 (en.Wikipedia 'Union Station (Brattleboro)', Lindsell p.173). 1877-1879 is deliberately left undrawn because no source names who ran the trains. Headway is an ESTIMATE: no timetable for this era was read for frequency.
sources: Segment-level: 1873 = rename convention of vermont_central_railroad.geojson; 1876 end from American-Rails.com and de.Wikipedia (1877), conflicting with en.Wikipedia Union Station (1880); Fowler 1876 Pathfinder column confirms the stops. Headway not sourced.

segments.note: Operated by the Connecticut River Railroad under a 50-year agency agreement 'from July 1, 1880' (ICC valuation); the CRR owned 99% of the Vermont Valley's stock. en.Wikipedia 'Union Station (Brattleboro)' (Lindsell p.173): 'in 1880, the Connecticut River Railroad obtained control of the CV mainline between Brattleboro and White River Junction'. Day conflict only: the parallel Sullivan agreement is dated 31 Aug 1880 (ICC). Springfield - Brattleboro - Bellows Falls - Windsor became one CRR-controlled route; Central Vermont trains continued over the line by trackage rights (ICC), which is not operation of the line, so no Central Vermont feature for these years. No timetable snapshot inside 1880-1892 was read; continuity is inferred on an active through route. Ends when the agreement was assigned to the Boston and Maine, which has operated the property 'since January 1, 1893' (ICC). Headway is an ESTIMATE: no timetable for this era was read for frequency.
sources: Segment-level: 1 July 1880 start and 1 Jan 1893 end from the ICC valuation report; 1880 also from en.Wikipedia Union Station (Lindsell p.173). Headway not sourced.

segments.note: Boston and Maine's Connecticut River Line (Springfield - White River Junction), operated by the B&M from 1 January 1893 under the Connecticut River RR's agency agreement (ICC); the B&M's direct lease of the Vermont Valley (1 Jan 1925) and the 1949 merger did not change who ran the trains. Central Vermont trains also used the line by trackage rights. Second main track Putney - Bellows Falls built 1901-03 (ICC). The September 1951 Official Guide (Table 16) shows rail times at Brattleboro and Putney (and, by position, Bellows Falls), including Washington/New York - Montreal through cars (the Montrealer/Washingtonian, drawn separately in montrealer.geojson). Fowler's B&M public timetables: Dummerston, East Putney and Grout (a flag stop by 1906) last listed 1932; Putney and Westminster still 1953. Passenger service ended in September 1966 with the end of the Montrealer: 6 Sept per en.Wikipedia 'Bellows Falls station', 3/4 Sept per other research; year firm. Freight continued (B&M, then Central Vermont from 1988, New England Central from 1994/95) and is not drawn; Amtrak's Montrealer restored passenger trains from 30 Sept 1972 and is drawn as amtrak-90 in amtrak.geojson. Headway is an ESTIMATE: the 1951 Guide shows about five trains each way at Brattleboro but the OCR is too mangled to separate daily from non-daily trains.
sources: Segment-level: 1893 start from the ICC valuation; service in Sept 1951 from the Official Guide Feb 1952 Table 16; Fowler's 1906/1921/1932/1953 B&M timetable columns; 1966 end from en.Wikipedia 'Union Station (Brattleboro)' (Lindsell p.175) and 'Bellows Falls station'. Headway not sourced.
